item.title: Spin SYK-dot chains: entanglement bound and resource estimates towards a quantum advantage
item.description:
📚 arXiv
👤 Sayantan Dey, Abel Carreras, Siddhartha Patra
arXiv:2611.03207v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Ground states of Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev (SYK)-type models are volume-law entangled, which makes them costly both for tensor networks and for quantum hardware simulations. Thus, it remains unclear where quantum hardware could outperform classical simulation of such models. In this work, we study a spin SYK-dot chain, in which q dense SYK dots of p qubits are joined by single ZZ bonds of strength K. The entanglement across any cut is then bounded by floor(p/2) ln 2 plus the inter-dot entanglement, and the two-qubit depth of one Trotter step is set by p alone. arXiv:2601.19765v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We present a new geometric perspective on quantum error correction based on spectral triples in noncommutative geometry. Locality, code distance, and the Knill Laflamme condition acquire a unified spectral and geometric interpretation in terms of the induced metric and spectrum of the Dirac operator. arXiv:2611.03128v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In quantum error correction, the decoder must estimate the errors from the measurement data accurately and fast enough to avoid a backlog. Search-based decoders such as Tesseract achieve high accuracy by finding a minimum-weight set of error events with an A* search, but their search effort grows rapidly with the physical error rate and the code size. arXiv:2611.03469v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Continuous blind stabilizer measurements turn stabilizer codes into a Liouvillian spectral problem in which Hamiltonian terms compete with dissipative error channels. arXiv:2611.02425v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum channel relative entropy can be nonadditive, making its regularization essential for asymptotic analysis. Notably, a simple two-copy additivity test distinguishes between these alternatives for qubit channels and for channel pairs in arbitrary dimensions admitting an interior optimizer. item.title: Entanglement in quantum spin chains is strictly finite at any temperature
item.description:
📚 arXiv
👤 Ainesh Bakshi, Soonwon Choi, Saúl Pilatowsky-Cameo
arXiv:2602.13386v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Entanglement is the hallmark of quantum physics, yet its characterization in interacting many-body systems at thermal equilibrium remains one of the most important challenges in quantum statistical physics. We prove that the Gibbs state of any quantum spin chain can be exactly decomposed into a mixture of matrix product states with a bond dimension that is independent of the system size, at any nonzero temperature. As a consequence, the Schmidt number, arguably the most stringent measure of bipartite entanglement, is strictly finite for thermal states, even in the thermodynamic limit. Our decomposition is explicit and is accompanied by an efficient classical algorithm to sample the resulting matrix product states.
